note: Drafted from the BRD's detector list. NOT signed off by anyone with Indian employment-law standing - see spec section 11.

categories.label: Marital status
categories.alternative: Ask about availability for the shift pattern instead: "This role runs rotational shifts - does that work for you?"

categories.label: Children and family planning
categories.alternative: Ask only about the job: "The role needs weekend coverage twice a month. Is that something you can commit to?"

categories.label: Pregnancy
categories.alternative: Never ask. If leave policy comes up, state the policy without asking about the candidate's plans.

categories.label: Age
categories.alternative: Ask about experience directly: "How many years have you spent in frontline retail sales?"

categories.label: Religion
categories.alternative: If availability on festival days matters, state the requirement: "The store trades on public holidays - are you able to work them?"

categories.label: Caste, community or native place
categories.alternative: If a language is genuinely required, ask about the language: "This branch serves Marathi-speaking customers - how comfortable are you selling in Marathi?"

categories.label: Gender-role assumption
categories.alternative: Put the requirement to every candidate the same way: "The role involves travel to three stores a week. Can you do that?"

categories.label: Disability or health
categories.alternative: Ask about the task, not the body: "The role needs standing for most of an eight-hour shift. Can you do that, with or without adjustments?"

categories.label: Salary history
categories.alternative: Ask for expectations against the band: "The band for this role is X to Y. Does that work for you?" Salary history is banned in 22 US states; in India it is legal but it imports the candidate's previous underpayment into your offer.
